title: Mechanical adaptations of form are demonstrable, unlike colour adaptations

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Mechanical adaptations of form are demonstrable, unlike colour adaptations

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Unlike explanations of colouration as cryptic, warning or mimetic, which cannot be demonstrated, the fitness of organic form for mechanical functions such as swimming or flight can be analysed and established in detail by statics and dynamics.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XVI: On Form and Mechanical Efficiency

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: But of a very different order from all such “adaptations” as these, are those very perfect adaptations of form which, for instance, fit a fish for swimming or a bird for flight. Here we are far above the region of mere hypothesis, for we have to deal with questions of mechanical efficiency where statical and dynamical considerations can be applied and established in detail.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter XVI, “On Form and Mechanical Efficiency”; topic “Mechanical fitness versus speculative adaptation”. Scope: adaptive form and colouration of animals in general

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch16-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.46

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Mechanical efficiency is empirically measurable, but the categorical contrast with all cryptic, warning and mimetic explanations needs substantial reinterpretation. Existing data can compare selected cases only.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define demonstrability as out-of-sample predictive performance of mechanical morphology models versus coloration-function models across species, and compare effect sizes and uncertainty. This tests the contrast, though not the philosophical assertion in full.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
“Can be demonstrated” is epistemic rather than a single biological variable.

Evidence quality differs for reasons unrelated to inherent testability.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

discriminating power: 0.35

operationalizability: 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Biomechanical performance of fins or wings can be modelled, and those models do not decide whether colour explanations are undemonstrable. The sentence is a methodological ranking of kinds of argument. Existing performance datasets leave that ranking untouched.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: The claim asserts that mechanical fitness of form can be demonstrated by statics and dynamics while cryptic, warning and mimetic colouration cannot. No measurement of organisms distinguishes that epistemic contrast from the rival view that both kinds of adaptation are demonstrable to similar standards.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value: Demonstrability is a standard of evidence, and colour hypotheses and mechanical hypotheses fail or succeed under different criteria.
